about: Generated by generate_vectors.py; do not edit by hand. TEST KEYS ONLY: every key but one is derived from its seed_text (seed = SHA-256 of the text; Ed25519: the seed is the private key; ECDSA P-256: the scalar is the seed as a big-endian integer mod (n - 1), plus 1); the RSA key is the 2048-bit test key RFC 9500, section 2.1, publishes as testRSA2048, given here by its public modulus and exponent. Records R0 to R2 and links L0 to L2 are those of the portable verification cases. Exports are portable verification 0.3.0 exports, their entries unsigned. Each checkpoint names the test key it was signed with (signed_with) and gives signed_bytes_hex, the bytes a verifier builds from it under the shared rule, and, where the key signed something else, signature_made_over_hex. cp_accented's chain_id is not ASCII: its length prefix counts 19 UTF-8 bytes, not 17 characters. Each token gives imprint_of_hex, the bytes its messageImprint is the SHA-256 of. A document's bytes as received (for attachment_digest and export_digest) are its JSON with no whitespace, in UTF-8.

scitt.about: A test SCITT transparency service (RFC 9943), test keys only. A statement is a tagged COSE_Sign1 (RFC 9052) by a witness key whose payload is the checkpoint's signed bytes under the shared rule, with its key_ref field equal to kid; the protected header has alg -19 (Ed25519, RFC 9864), kid, and the CWT claims (RFC 9597, label 15) iss, the key's holder, and sub, the chain. A receipt (RFC 9942) is a tagged COSE_Sign1 by a service key over the RFC 9162 SHA-256 tree's root, its payload detached, with the verifiable data structure (label 395, value 1) in the protected header and the inclusion proof [tree-size, leaf-index, path] (label 396, key -1) in the unprotected one. A leaf's data is the statement's bytes as registered, tag included; its hash is SHA-256(0x00 || data). to_be_signed_hex is the Sig_structure each signature was made over.

opentimestamps.about: OpenTimestamps proofs. The real one (real_r0) is described where REAL_OTS_PROOF_B64 is set in generate_vectors.py; its headers are mainnet's, as two explorers gave them. Every other proof leads to a synthetic header (synthetic_header): a test block with no proof of work, holding the proof's result as its Merkle root in the header's own byte order. A header set is what a verifier holds from its own source; header_sources is the policy entry naming that source.
